provenance: Author-side interpretation of retained detailed sections, existing objective-controls and constructed cases; 2026-11-27; AI-assisted; not an independent review.

limitations.SEDI-BOR-02: API and policy checks miss undocumented override paths and post-assessment changes; authority must be exercised within scope.
limitations.SEDI-BOR-08: Bounded attribute combinations and payload/side-channel tests cannot establish complete cryptographic hiding; policy review cannot verify enforcement.
limitations.SEDI-BOR-10: Tested code and point-in-time review cannot rule out covert logging, firmware changes or inaccurate attestations.
limitations.SEDI-PRG-01: Component and point-in-time assessment cannot cover emergent integration failures or regressions; documents do not establish live behavior.
limitations.SEDI-PRG-02: Publication and link checks do not establish independent implementability; expert sufficiency judgments are bounded.
limitations.SEDI-PRG-04: Administrative timing evidence depends on accurate records and does not rule out retrospectively altered dates.
limitations.SEDI-PRG-05: Published replies alone cannot establish that material comments were substantively addressed.
limitations.SEDI-SDI-01: Conformance tests cannot establish propagation delay across deployed verifiers; documentation does not verify status correctness.
limitations.SEDI-SDI-02: Workflow tests cannot establish that all recovery paths avoid reproofing or meet holder needs; identifier rebinding remains technical evidence.
limitations.SEDI-SDI-03: Known-model tests do not exclude statistical linkage through rare attributes or timing; administrative review is not cryptographic proof.
limitations.SEDI-SDI-06: Lab offline tests cannot exhaust degraded connectivity conditions; subsequent protocol changes may introduce regressions.
limitations.SEDI-SDI-07: Finite adversary models do not exclude side-channel or implementation-specific disclosure; structural omission does not by itself establish cryptographic hiding.
limitations.SEDI-SDI-10: Automated checks cannot establish usability or cognitive burden; representative user studies may miss affected populations.
limitations.SEDI-SDI-17: Network observations and known threat models cannot rule out hidden or out-of-band monitoring; policy assertions cannot establish architectural absence.
limitations.SEDI-SDI-23: An allowed reason code does not substantiate the actual ground; retrospective review cannot prevent improper revocation.
limitations.SEDI-SDI-24: Simulated triggers and periodic reviews cannot establish complete breach detection or timely response to novel or insider incidents.
limitations.SEDI-APP-02: Workflow checks cannot authenticate guardianship documents or cover all relationship and emancipation edge cases.
limitations.SEDI-APP-03: Identity and consent checks do not establish all legal relationship and substituted-decision conditions; periodic review is not runtime evidence.
limitations.SEDI-APP-04: Administrative records cannot reveal every informal enrollment prerequisite or local possession assumption.
limitations.SEDI-GOV-01: Design and records cannot establish parity in actual counter behavior, fees and processing times across locations.
limitations.SEDI-GOV-02: Periodic assessment cannot detect all localized or informal physical-ID denial or establish complaint effectiveness.
limitations.SEDI-GOV-05: Administrative evidence does not independently establish infeasibility; expert feasibility judgments and exception scope require case-specific review.
limitations.SEDI-WAL-09: Tested guardian relationship types and point-in-time policy review do not establish authorization correctness across all runtime actions.
limitations.SEDI-WAL-12: A recorded prompt and affirmative action do not establish informed choice; UI changes and runtime consent flows need separate evidence.
limitations.SEDI-WAL-14: Testing cannot exhaust hidden server-side retention and sharing; policy review does not prove runtime deletion.
limitations.SEDI-VER-05: Finite tests of relationship types and periodic review do not establish valid, current representative authority at each presentation.
limitations.SEDI-RPY-05: Representative acceptance tests cannot cover all relationships or evolving service offerings; policy review does not establish equivalent live treatment.
limitations.SEDI-LOY-01: Pattern matching cannot establish absence of contextual manipulation; UX review is subjective and point-in-time.
limitations.SEDI-LOY-02: Exploitation requires contextual judgment about conduct and incentives; policy and technical review cannot detect all external business practices.
limitations.SEDI-LOY-03: Known vulnerability tests cannot establish proportionality of risk and benefit; risk conditions change between reviews.
limitations.SEDI-LOY-04: Detriment depends on factual outcomes; administrative review cannot detect unreported harms.
limitations.SEDI-LOY-05: Harm can manifest outside the identity system or go unreported; technical success is not evidence of its absence.
limitations.SEDI-ENF-03: Log infrastructure checks do not establish substantive audit coverage or continued completeness through the audit date.
limitations.SEDI-ENF-04: Network checks cannot rule out side-channel, telemetry or operational-log disclosure; architectural changes can invalidate prior review.
limitations.SEDI-PRV-01: Rare attribute combinations and unmodeled attacks remain outside bounded unlinkability tests; administrative evidence cannot replace cryptographic examination.
limitations.SEDI-PRV-03: Runtime observations cannot establish absence of covert correlation channels; architectural review is point-in-time.
limitations.SEDI-PRV-04: Deletion tests do not establish minimization across organizations and lifecycle stages; undocumented collection may escape review.
limitations.SEDI-INT-01: Catalog checks miss uncataloged interfaces; the source labels EXPT N/A while its limitation calls for expert review.
limitations.SEDI-INT-02: Common encoding tests do not exhaust verifier implementations or capture implementation drift between modes.
limitations.SEDI-INT-03: Finite wallet-pair tests and specification review cannot establish portability across all implementations.
limitations.SEDI-INT-04: Negative tests cover only enumerated downgrade paths and point-in-time design; ADMN applicability is undeclared, not N/A.
limitations.SEDI-KMS-04: Rotation schedules do not establish cryptographic correctness; the source marks EXPT N/A while its limitation calls for expert review of overlap.
limitations.SEDI-KMS-05: Plan records and tabletop exercises do not establish response to real compromises.

context_groups.context: People choosing or needing a physical pathway, including those without a compatible device or with accessibility needs
context_groups.reason: Access, cost and time must remain comparable without compelling digital enrollment; a policy alone may conceal local denial.

context_groups.context: People presenting limited attributes or credentials across unrelated services
context_groups.reason: Attribute leakage, correlation and latent observation can expose people beyond the intended transaction.

context_groups.context: People declining secondary use or facing a changed request, incompatible verifier or downstream processor
context_groups.reason: Consent at one component does not establish the purpose, recipient, retention or privacy properties of the completed interaction.

context_groups.context: Holders recovering from device loss, migrating wallets, or disputing revocation; verifiers with stale status material
context_groups.reason: Lifecycle transitions can lock out legitimate holders or accept compromised credentials even where components pass nominal checks.

context_groups.context: Non-emancipated minors, people needing representation, designated representatives and subjects affected by a conflicted representative
context_groups.reason: Identity authentication, relationship authority, action scope, continued validity and the person's preferences are distinct.

context_groups.context: Applicants dependent on authoritative source data and accessible proofing or correction
context_groups.reason: Incorrect upstream data, disproportionate proofing and stale provider authorization can exclude eligible applicants or falsely flag them.

context_groups.context: Holders at contactless service points and people seeking services from qualifying health care providers
context_groups.reason: Lab interoperability or a general optional-acceptance rule does not establish actual service acceptance under the applicable actor obligations.

context_groups.context: Independent implementers, verifiers relying on profile claims, holders using online/offline modes and assessors
context_groups.reason: Version, hook, role and mode mismatch can invalidate a component-level claim at the interaction boundary.

context_groups.context: Department approving profiles, independent assessors, auditors and people relying on continuing conformance
context_groups.reason: Technical success, administrative approval, complete evidence and changes to a deployed configuration must be assessed separately.

context_groups.context: Holders relying on authentic issuance and continuity, Department key operators and delegated infrastructure operators
context_groups.reason: Key provenance, custody, current operational authorization and privilege termination affect holders even where technical checks pass.
